title: No reader doc states the basis of the identification heat-loss figure; it sits 18.9 % below heat_loss_w_per_k
claim: The Learning Model Status sensor publishes two heat-loss figures on different bases (heat_loss_w_per_k on the effective loss house_heat_loss_base x scale; system_identification.heat_loss_kw_per_c on the configured zone total U+L), and of the 5 reader-document units that describe the identification loss coefficient none states its basis, although on the two-zone test profile with a learned lower-floor ratio of 1.4 the two bases differ by 18.9 %.
mechanism: sysid:_zone_heat_loss returns upper_floor_heat_loss + lower_floor_heat_loss (configured), while thermal_model:ThermalParameters.house_heat_loss_base uses lower_floor_heat_loss_learned; payload.py and sysid.py comments name the basis, but README.md (Learning Model Status row, line 623) and docs/how-it-works.md 'Active system identification' (lines 1197-1265) speak of 'the loss coefficient' with no basis, so a reader comparing the identification figure with the W/K figure on the same sensor sees an unexplained gap.

evidence.contention_note: box heavily loaded (load1 ~150); ratio and counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --doc-fix: one sentence naming the basis (configured zone total vs heat_loss_w_per_k's effective loss) added in memory to how-it-works.md's identification section

null_control.note: with the lower-floor ratio at 1 the two bases coincide and the missing statement costs the reader nothing; the gap is the learned split's

metric_definition: Relative gap (effective - zone_total)/zone_total of the two published heat-loss bases on the two-zone profile; count of identification heat-loss units in README+docs stating a basis.
phenomenon_property: Every reader-document unit that describes a published figure with more than one possible basis (configured vs effective heat loss) states which basis it is on.
proposed_fix_scope: One sentence in how-it-works.md 'Active system identification' (and the README Learning Model Status row) saying the identification loss coefficient is on the configured zone total U+L and reads below heat_loss_w_per_k (the effective loss) once the learned lower-floor ratio leaves 1. For D6: the sentence's truth against sysid.py.
